extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, their counsel, and USPTO/OED staff handling disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order approving a settlement agreement resolving disciplinary action against a registered patent practitioner under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, describing stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions and procedures for enforcement and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over the matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory and regulatory provisions authorize the Office to pursue and approve disciplinary actions and settlement agreements against registered practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, as a registered patent attorney, is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct set forth at 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners are bound by the full suite of professional conduct rules in evaluating fitness to practice and determining sanctions for misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited: criminal act reflecting adversely on fitness (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Committing a criminal act that reflects adversely on the practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness, or fitness as a practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example on this record: pleading guilty to leaving the scene of an accident involving personal injury is treated as a violation of § 11.804(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited: other conduct adversely reflecting on fitness (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example on this record: driving while intoxicated, causing a traffic accident in which a person was injured, and leaving the scene constituted a violation of § 11.804(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension as agreed sanction (six months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for a period of six months, commencing nunc pro tunc to the date of interim suspension, July 31, 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order implements the agreed suspension term as the primary disciplinary sanction for the misconduct described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued suspension until reinstatement petition granted (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the Office until the OED Director grants Respondent's petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires compliance with the procedures and standards of § 11.60 and affirmative action by the OED Director to restore practice privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section citations impose obligations such as reporting convictions and following reinstatement procedures; compliance is a condition of the settlement and any petition for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period (five years concurrent with state probation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a five-year probationary period running concurrently with the probation imposed by the Virginia State Court in the related criminal case, commencing February 8, 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation runs contemporaneously with the criminal probation and is part of the disciplinary outcome to monitor future conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for alleged probation/Agreement violation: Order to Show Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with the Agreement, Final Order, or any disciplinary rule during the probationary period, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause why Respondent should not be immediately suspended for up to an additional six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order to Show Cause will be sent to Respondent at the last address of record furnished to the OED Director and initiates the administrative enforcement process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and response timeline for Order to Show Cause (15 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be granted fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause after it is sent to the last address of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives Respondent a defined short period to contest the alleged violations before the OED Director moves forward with recommendations to the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director referral to USPTO Director with evidence and request for additional suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If after the 15-day response period the OED Director remains of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director: (i) the Order to Show Cause; (ii) Respondent's response, if any; and (iii) argument and evidence supporting the OED Director's opinion, and request that the USPTO Director immediately suspend Respondent for up to an additional six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the evidentiary referral and recommendation step in seeking further suspension from the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional suspension not stayed by review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director suspends Respondent pursuant to the OED referral and Respondent seeks review of the additional suspension, any such review shall not operate to postpone or hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative or judicial review will not automatically delay the effect of an imposed additional suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room, ensuring public access to the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice with prescribed content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided template describing the suspension, probation, underlying misconduct, and violated provisions of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must include practitioner identification (name, registration number, location), a summary of misconduct (e.g., operated vehicle while intoxicated, caused injury, left scene), and citation of violated rules (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) and § 11.804(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding when addressing further complaints or evidence of similar misconduct, in future disciplinary proceedings as an aggravating factor or rebuttal, or in connection with requests for reconsideration of reinstatement decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be used to increase sanctions in later proceedings, rebut statements by Respondent, or inform reconsideration determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to fully comply with § 11.60 on any reinstatement request
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must fully comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full compliance with the reinstatement regulation is a precondition to being considered for restoration of practice privileges.
